name: AWS STS AssumeRole Chaining - Pivot Across Roles/Accounts
description: Use sts:AssumeRole to hop from one IAM role to another, chaining across roles and even AWS accounts to reach higher privilege. Over-broad trust policies, wildcard principals, and missing or guessable sts:ExternalId conditions create confused-deputy and cross-account escalation paths. Role chaining also lets an attacker launder their identity and shorten the audit trail.
notes:
=== WHAT ENABLES IT ===
  A role's trust policy (AssumeRolePolicyDocument) lists who may assume it.
  Over-broad principals ( "AWS": "*" , a whole account root, or a role you
  already control) let you assume higher-priv roles, possibly cross-account.

=== FIND ASSUMABLE ROLES ===
  aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[].{Name:RoleName,Trust:AssumeRolePolicyDocument}'
  # or enumerate with Pacu / pmapper to graph who-can-assume-what

=== ASSUME A ROLE ===
  aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/<priv_role> \
    --role-session-name pivot
  # export the returned AccessKeyId/SecretAccessKey/SessionToken, then:
  aws sts get-caller-identity

=== CROSS-ACCOUNT WITH EXTERNAL ID (confused deputy) ===
  aws sts assume-role --role-arn arn:aws:iam::<other_acct>:role/<role> \
    --role-session-name pivot --external-id <external_id>
  # if the ExternalId is weak/guessable/leaked, the control fails

=== CHAINING (role -> role -> role) ===
  # assume role A, configure it as a profile, then assume role B from it:
  aws configure set profile.a.aws_access_key_id ...
  aws sts assume-role --profile a --role-arn arn:...:role/B --role-session-name b
  # note: chained sessions are capped at 1 hour

=== USE A NAMED PROFILE (role_arn + source_profile) ===
  ~/.aws/config:
    [profile pivot]
    role_arn = arn:aws:iam::<acct>:role/<priv_role>
    source_profile = default

=== NEXT ===
  After landing in the target role, enumerate and look for the next hop.

defense.why_it_works: AssumeRole is governed entirely by the target role's trust policy. When that policy names an over-broad principal (account root, wildcard, or a role the attacker controls) or relies on a weak/guessable ExternalId, an attacker can legitimately assume a more privileged role, including across accounts.
defense.prerequisites: Control of a principal that is trusted by the target role (directly or via a chain), plus sts:AssumeRole; for cross-account confused-deputy, knowledge of (or absence of) the required ExternalId.
defense.impact: Privilege escalation and cross-account/cross-boundary movement; attacker obtains the target role's permissions and can continue chaining toward administrative access while obscuring their original identity.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1078.004] CloudTrail AssumeRole events where the assuming identity is itself an assumed-role session (chaining), cross-account AssumeRole from unexpected source accounts/IPs, or a burst of AssumeRole calls walking multiple roles.
defense.artifacts: CloudTrail AssumeRole events with userIdentity.type=AssumedRole as the caller, requestParameters.roleArn, requestParameters.externalId, and resources showing the target role; sts:GetCallerIdentity probes.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=aws sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail eventName=AssumeRole
| stats count values(requestParameters.roleArn) as roles dc(requestParameters.roleArn) as nroles by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| where nroles>2
defense.sentinel_kql:
AWSCloudTrail
| where EventName == "AssumeRole"
| where UserIdentityType == "AssumedRole"
| summarize Roles=dcount(tostring(parse_json(RequestParameters).roleArn)), Calls=count() by UserIdentityArn, SourceIpAddress
| where Roles > 2
defense.prevention: Scope every role trust policy to specific principals (no account-root or wildcard); require a strong unique sts:ExternalId for third-party cross-account roles; add aws:SourceArn/aws:SourceAccount conditions; use permission boundaries and SCPs to cap reachable privilege; alert on role chaining and unexpected cross-account AssumeRole.

detections.name: STS role chaining / cross-account AssumeRole
detections.logic:
index=aws sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail eventName=AssumeRole userIdentity.type=AssumedRole
| stats dc(requestParameters.roleArn) as roles values(requestParameters.roleArn) as chain by userIdentity.arn, sourceIPAddress
| where roles>2
detections.false_positives: Legitimate automation that chains roles (CI/CD, cross-account tooling)
detections.tuning: Baseline normal role-assumption graphs per principal; alert on new cross-account targets or chains deeper than expected
